episodes.212466: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening of June 2 across central and north central South Dakota. The storms produced golf ball-sized hail five miles southwest of the Counselor Creek Recreation Area and quarter-sized hail two miles north of Hoven. The COOP observer near Artas recorded an 80 mph wind gust on a personal weather station, which damaged a swing set and knocked a camper off its cinderblocks. Additionally, the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station nine miles north-northwest of Vivian recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
episodes.212498: A slow moving upper level disturbance over northern Mexico and the Desert Southwest combined with moist surface southeast flow resulting in thunderstorm development across central and eastern New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours. Some storms resulted in severe hail at Chacon, severe thunderstorm wind gusts near Sumner Lake and Endee on June 2nd and some burn scar flash flooding in Ruidoso on June 3rd.
episodes.212562: A thunderstorm moving through Richland county briefly became severe near Sioux Pass.
episodes.212701: A severe thunderstorm tracked across northern Denver and nearby suburbs producing hail up to 1.75 inch in diameter. Additional severe thunderstorms brought hail up to 2 inch in diameter to the eastern Colorado plains.
episodes.212955: A cold front moved into the area just before midnight on 6/1 with a moderately unstable air mass in place with MLCAPE values around 1000 J/kg. With deep layer shear between 20-30 knots, organized storms produced mostly sub severe wind gusts with two reports of damage associated with severe wind gusts.
episodes.213270: During the afternoon and evening of June 2, thunderstorm development was initiated by a weak backdoor cold front moving in from the northeast. The resulting activity was primarily concentrated within and surrounding the DFW Metroplex, leading to instances of marginally severe hail and strong to severe thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.213278: From June 2-4, 2026, a series of disturbances tracking across the region within broad zonal flow set off several rounds of thunderstorms to the region. A slow-moving front on June 2 set off the first round of thunderstorms, producing widespread heavy rain and localized flash flooding. The most significant impacts occurred in Oglala and surrounding communities, where 6 to 7 inches of rain fell in a short period, causing streets and ditches to fill extremely quickly. Some storms also produced large hail and strong winds. Some storms also produced large hail and strong winds.||June 3 brought another round of storms as a disturbance moved across the Northern Plains. Clearing over Wyoming and the Black Hills allowed storms to redevelop along a boundary across southern South Dakota. Several became supercells, including the storm that produced the rain-wrapped Ideal tornado in Tripp County. The tornado mainly affected agricultural land but damaged multiple outbuildings and caused additional RFD���related damage to a nearby modular home.||On June 4, the severe threat was more limited. Lower dewpoints over Wyoming and a strong cap over the Black Hills and western South Dakota kept storm coverage down, though a few storms still became severe with larger hail and strong wind gusts. A landspout also occurred in northeast Wyoming with one of the isolated storms.
episodes.213429: A line of strong to severe storms marched eastward out of southwestern Kansas and into south-central Kansas during late night hours of June 1 and the early morning hours of June 2. These storms produced wind gusts around 70 to 90 mph across portions of Kingman County, and wind gusts up to 60 mph across portions of Sedgwick and Sumner Counties. Damage to structures occurred across southern Kingman County.
episodes.213744: Showers and thunderstorms affected the combined Panhandles each afternoon and evening in the early parts of June. With enough moisture, instability and sources to provide atmospheric lift, these storms were able to become severe each day and bring large hail to the region. A few instances of damaging winds and flooding also occurred.
episodes.213797: During the early morning hours of June 2, 2026, scattered, pulse-type thunderstorms developed and hail and heavy rainfall to portions of southeast Nebraska. Based on radar analysis, the most intense hail core tracked directly over Lincoln, Nebraska, resulting in a public report of quarter-size (1.00 inch) hail. In addition to the hail threat, these thunderstorms were highly efficient rainfall producers. The combination of intense rainfall rates and slow storm motions allowed a quick 2 to 3 inches of rain to accumulate across localized areas of southeast Nebraska.
episodes.213973: As an upper level low moved through the region, severe thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front that moved through North Dakota. Scattered showers and non-severe thunderstorms were ongoing during the morning before increasing in strength throughout the afternoon. A cluster of severe thunderstorms moved through parts of north central North Dakota, including the Turtle Mountains area, before additional storms developed to the south in the James River Valley area. |The most significant damage occurred approximately 4 miles northeast of Belcourt. Multiple buildings were damaged at a collection of properties in this area. A garage on the southwest side of the damage area lost a section of its roof that video and drone footage show was blown northeast across the property. The other main building with damage is a residential home at the center property that lost a significant portion of its roof ripped off. On the north and east side of this property, there were multiple hardwood trees damaged, some snapped about halfway down, but all generally extending to the northeast. A utility truck was parked at the center property and was facing south when the storm came through. A two by four plank of wood went through the windshield and both occupants of the truck had minor injuries. At the eastern property in this group, a shed collapsed and was blown into the edge of a wooded area to the northeast. Drone footage shows numerous trees damaged in this wooded area, extending a few hundred feet northeast of the buildings on the property. Winds were estimated at 95 mph. To the northeast, there was another property with approximately 15 to 20 oak trees that were damaged. |The other main area of damage occurred in Stutsman County, one mile west of Spiritwood. A 200 foot by 60 foot barn was blown over and dismantled. Based on photo and satellite imagery, barn was oriented west-east with 3 doors facing south. The storm was moving from south to north, which would be a favorable direction to funnel wind into the broad side of the barn with multiple doors, helping the barn collapse and push pieces into the tree row directly to the north. This is consistent with wind speeds of around 85 mph.|The highest measured wind gust was 62 mph near Zeeland in Mcintosh County and near Pettibone in Kidder County. The largest hail reported was golf ball sized, west of Belcourt in Rolette County.
episodes.214096: Severe storms produced hail over the Houston Metro area.
episodes.214340: A mature mesoscale convective system (MCS) impacted portions of far northern Oklahoma during the very late evening of the 1st into the early morning hours of the 2nd. Several severe wind gusts were observed across this area during that time.
episodes.214359: A remnant outflow boundary extended roughly west-to-east from North Central Texas into Northeast Texas and far Northwest Louisiana early in the afternoon on June 2nd, with a separate convective outflow boundary analyzed to the north across Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas. South of this secondary outflow boundary, temperatures were in the lower 90s F with lower to mid 70s dew points supportive of strong buoyancy characterized by MLCAPE values 3000-3500+ J/kg. High precipitable water (PWAT) values of 1.7+ inches within the unstable environment supported strong downdrafts capable of isolated damaging wind gusts. As a result, thunderstorms increased in coverage through the afternoon along these boundaries with several damaging wind reports recorded across parts of Southwest Arkansas.
episodes.214466: Clusters of strong thunderstorms along the coast and offshore produced a few measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.214476: A remnant outflow boundary extended roughly west-to-east from North Central Texas into Northeast Texas and far Northwest Louisiana early in the afternoon on June 2nd, with a separate convective outflow boundary analyzed to the north across Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas. As a result, thunderstorms increased in coverage through the afternoon along these boundaries with several damaging wind reports recorded across parts of Northwest Louisiana along with a few reports of localized flash flooding.
episodes.214480: A remnant outflow boundary extended roughly west-to-east from North Central Texas into Northeast Texas and far Northwest Louisiana early in the afternoon on June 2nd, with a separate convective outflow boundary analyzed to the north across Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas. High precipitable water (PWAT) values of 1.7+ inches within the unstable environment supported strong downdrafts capable of isolated damaging wind gusts. As a result, thunderstorms increased in coverage through the afternoon along these boundaries with several damaging wind reports recorded across parts of East Texas.
episodes.214506: A trough axis extending from the eastern Great Lakes into the Mid-Atlantic states and a ridge centered over the central and southern Plains placed the forecast area directly between both features.  A weak front approached the area from the north.   This front was the initial focal point for convective activity to begin developing in the afternoon hours.  This activity capitalized on a warm, moist, and unstable environment to produce slow moving strong thunderstorms in the Baton Rouge area.  These storms produce isolated flash flooding and severe wind gusts.
episodes.214510: Weak sea breeze boundaries beneath a broad and deep area of high pressure served as a focal point for convective initiation.  A warm, moist, and unstable environment allowed a few of the storms to produce severe marine wind gusts.
episodes.214567: A severe line of storms swept across most of Alabama from north to south, causing numerous trees and power lines to fall across the state.  Southeast Alabama was not spared and saw numerous reports of downed trees and lines.
episodes.214615: A line of severe storms that produced widespread wind damage in Alabama moved into the Florida panhandle and gradually weakened but not before producing a few more reports of wind damage.
episodes.214616: A line of severe storms that produced widespread wind damage in Alabama moved into southwest Georgia and gradually weakened, but not before producing a few more reports of wind damage.
episodes.214675: On the afternoon of June 2nd, a weak disturbance passing through the region promoted isolated thunderstorms along the higher elevations of West Virginia. While the majority of these storms remained under severe strength, a small quadrant of activity in McDowell County yielded downed trees and power lines due to damaging wind gusts. Otherwise, high pressure influenced the lowlands and maintained quiet weather.
episodes.214676: A stationary boundary draped across Arkansas in tandem with a high CAPE, low shear environment would set up a region of significantly high DCAPE across central and southern Arkansas. The result would be multiple reports of large hail, but mostly damaging winds, including a downburst that impact locations south-southwest of the Little Rock metro.
episodes.214702: A weak surface trough moved in from the southeast and brought elevated moisture. Southeast winds allowed the south and eastern slopes of the Big Island to receive the most rain.
episodes.214728: A line of strong to severe storms organized over southwest Kentucky during the early morning hours of June 1, 2026. These storms moved south into West Tennessee and along the Tennessee River into northeast Mississippi during the morning hours. The storms fed on strong instability and adequate deep-layer shear to produce isolated wind damage and large hail. This first round of storms left behind an outflow boundary extending from eastern Arkansas across the Memphis metropolitan area into north Mississippi. Storms ignited along this boundary during the late afternoon and evening hours, fueled by strong instability and an upper-level trough overspreading the region. There were several additional reports of large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.214729: A line of strong to severe storms organized over southwest Kentucky during the early morning hours of June 1, 2026. The storms fed on strong instability and adequate deep-layer shear to produce isolated wind damage and large hail. This first round of storms left behind an outflow boundary extending from eastern Arkansas across the Memphis metropolitan area into north Mississippi. Storms ignited along this boundary during the late afternoon and evening hours, fueled by strong instability and an upper-level trough overspreading the region. episodes.214813: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed and moved northeast across northwest Kansas during the late afternoon and evening hours on the 1st. Hail up to quarter size and 58 mph winds were both reported in Sherman county.
episodes.214848: Severe thunderstorms occurs from late morning through the evening hours across the Devils Lake Basin and northeast North Dakota. Large hail to the size of golf balls was reported, and severe winds to 73 mph were measured.
episodes.214957: A line of thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours of June 1st over eastern Wyoming. As this line tracked east it produced strong straight line winds over northern Garden County. Wind gusts up to 62 MPH were reported at Crescent Lakes National Wildlife Refuge.
episodes.215147: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms moved east to northeast across east-central and northeast Colorado during the late afternoon and evening hours of June 1st. The highest wind gust was 64 mph in Yuma county, and the largest hail was one inch in diameter in Yuma and Kit Carson counties.
episodes.215154: Elevated showers developed in portions of central and southern Wyoming. Some produced strong wind gusts when they collapsed.
episodes.215588: Southeast surface flow helped bring in some modest moisture to the eastern Sacramento Mountains with south-southwest flow aloft resulting in wind shear across the area.  Strong storm develop around Mayhill and dropped hail up to 3.5 inches in diameter.
episodes.215610: Scattered afternoon storms developed across southeast Texas with a couple storms becoming severe.
episodes.215704: Severe storms developed on June 1st mostly across central and southern Mississippi as afternoon heating of a very moist airmass contributed to substantial atmospheric destabilization. The primary observed impacts were from damaging winds though at least one report of large hail was recorded. Additional thunderstorms developed in the afternoon of June 2nd in a similarly unstable summer airmass.
episodes.215729: Early summer environment of moderate shear and instability contributed to the development of strong storms that produced wind damage near Sebring in Highlands County.
episodes.215825: Strong thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts and hail along the coast.
episodes.215827: Strong thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts and hail in Volusia County.
episodes.215924: South Florida was in the warm sector of a surface frontal system with a broad area of high pressure over the eastern United States. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and evening hours over Southeast Florida and the adjacent waters.
episodes.216025: A lee convective cloud line extending west of Key West resulted in a waterspout well west of Key West, in the Marquesas Keys.
